quranUsage: Occurs 34 times, mostly as mīthāq, 'covenant': 'We took the covenant (mīthāqa) of the Children of Israel' (2:83), and 'We raised the mountain above you' when taking it (2:63). Breaking it is condemned: 'for their breaking of their covenant (mīthāqahum)' (4:155).

primaryMeaning: The side of something. Jānib is a side or flank; ijtanaba is to keep something to one side — to avoid it; junub is one who has been put aside from prayer until purified.
extendedMeaning: Junub, 'in a state of impurity', appears in the rulings of prayer and ablution (4:43). A soul will say, 'Alas for me, for what I neglected in regard to Allah (fī janbi Allāh)' (39:56).
quranUsage: Occurs 33 times. Ijtanaba, 'to avoid', is used for keeping away from wrong: 'avoid (ijtanibū) false gods' (16:36), and believers 'avoid (yajtanibūna) the major sins' (42:37). Jānib, 'side', appears in Musa being called 'from the right side (jānibi) of the Mount' (19:52).

primaryMeaning: To head towards something with purpose. Ḥajj is setting out for the House of Allah — the pilgrimage; ḥujja is an argument or proof, which heads straight for its goal; ḥājja is to argue.
extendedMeaning: 'To Allah belongs the conclusive argument (al-ḥujja al-bāligha)' (6:149).
quranUsage: Occurs 33 times. 'Complete the Hajj (al-ḥajj) and the ʿumra for Allah' (2:196), and 'pilgrimage to the House is a duty owed to Allah' (3:97). Ḥujja, 'argument': 'so that people will have no argument (ḥujjatun) against you' (2:150). Ibrahim argued with the king 'who argued (ḥājja) with him about his Lord' (2:258).

extendedMeaning: Surah 91 opens 'By the sun (wal-shams) and its brightness' (91:1). Prayer is to be established 'from the decline of the sun (al-shams)' (17:78). The Queen of Sheba's people 'prostrate to the sun (lil-shams)' (27:24).
quranUsage: Occurs 33 times, often as a sign of Allah's order: 'the sun (al-shams) runs to its resting place' (36:38), and 'it is not for the sun to overtake the moon' (36:40). Ibrahim, seeing the sun set, turned from worshipping created things (6:78). The sun too prostrates to Allah (22:18).

primaryMeaning: Shade — the cover that keeps off the sun's heat. Ẓill is shade or shadow; ẓulla is a canopy; ẓalla, 'to remain', is literally to spend the daytime doing something.
extendedMeaning: Ẓalla, 'to become': when told of a daughter, 'his face becomes (ẓalla) dark' (16:58). 'The mountain was raised above them like a canopy (ẓulla)' (7:171).
quranUsage: Occurs 33 times. 'We shaded you (ẓallalnā) with clouds' in the desert (2:57). The righteous in Paradise are 'in shades (ẓilālin)' (36:56) and 'extended shade (ẓillin mamdūd)' (56:30). The people of the Fire have 'coverings (ẓulalun) of fire above them' (39:16).

primaryMeaning: Something raised up and roofed — a canopy, a trellis, a roof. ʿArsh is a raised seat, a throne; ʿarsh Allāh is the Throne of Allah, the greatest of His creation.
extendedMeaning: Maʿrūshāt, 'trellised gardens', are among Allah's blessings (6:141). A town 'fallen down upon its roofs (ʿurūshihā)' describes utter ruin (2:259).
quranUsage: Occurs 33 times, mostly for the Throne: 'then He rose over the Throne (al-ʿarsh)' (7:54), 'Lord of the Great Throne' (9:129), and 'His Throne (ʿarshuhu) was upon the water' (11:7). It is also used for human thrones — the Queen of Sheba's (27:23).

primaryMeaning: Blindness — losing sight, and by extension losing insight, being unable to see the truth.
extendedMeaning: 'Whoever turns from My remembrance … We will raise him blind (aʿmā) on the Day of Resurrection' (20:124). Surah 80 begins with the Prophet frowning when 'the blind man (al-aʿmā) came to him' (80:2).
quranUsage: Occurs 33 times. The deniers are 'deaf, dumb and blind (ʿumyun)' (2:18) — unable to take in guidance. 'It is not the eyes that go blind (taʿmā), but the hearts in the breasts' (22:46). 'Are the blind (al-aʿmā) and the seeing equal?' (6:50).

primaryMeaning: To divide into parts. Qisma is a share. Aqsama, 'to swear', is traced by al-Rāghib to qasāma — oaths divided among the relatives of a murdered person.
extendedMeaning: The deniers' claim of daughters for Allah is 'an unjust division (qismatun ḍīzā)' (53:22). Relatives present at the division (al-qisma) of inheritance should be given something (4:8).
quranUsage: Occurs 33 times, mostly for oaths: 'I swear (uqsimu) by the positions of the stars' (56:75), and the deniers 'swore by Allah their strongest oaths' (6:109). Allah divides provision: 'We have divided (qasamnā) among them their livelihood' (43:32).

primaryMeaning: To be enough, to meet a need so nothing more is required.
extendedMeaning: 'We are sufficient for you (kafaynāka) against the mockers' (15:95).
quranUsage: Occurs 33 times, most often as wa kafā bi-llāh, 'Allah is sufficient', ending a verse: 'Allah is sufficient as Reckoner' (4:6), 'as Witness' (4:79), 'as Disposer of affairs' (4:81). 'Allah will suffice you (fa-sa-yakfīkahum) against them' (2:137). 'Is not Allah sufficient (bi-kāfin) for His servant?' (39:36).

primaryMeaning: Open land — barr is the dry land, as opposed to the sea. From its wide openness comes birr, 'righteousness' — broad, generous goodness in faith and deeds; barr is one who is dutiful and kind.
extendedMeaning: Yahya was 'dutiful (barran) to his parents' (19:14). Believers may 'deal kindly (tabarrūhum) and justly' with those who do not fight them (60:8). Barr, 'land': 'the game of the sea is lawful for you, but the game of the land (al-barr) is forbidden while in iḥrām' (5:96).
quranUsage: Occurs 32 times. Birr is defined in 2:177: 'righteousness (al-birr) is not that you turn your faces east or west, but it is believing in Allah … giving wealth … establishing prayer'. 'You will not attain righteousness (al-birr) until you spend from what you love' (3:92). Al-abrār, 'the righteous', are in bliss (76:5).

primaryMeaning: A camel kneeling and settling firmly on the ground. Baraka, 'blessing', is lasting good that settles in a thing and increases; tabāraka, 'blessed is He', is the praise of Allah's abundant good.
extendedMeaning: The land around al-Aqṣā is 'which We blessed (bāraknā) around it' (17:1). Surah 67 opens, 'Blessed is He (tabāraka) in whose hand is the dominion'.
quranUsage: Occurs 32 times. Tabāraka describes Allah: 'Blessed is Allah, Lord of the worlds' (7:54), 'Blessed is Allah, the best of creators' (23:14). Mubārak, 'blessed', describes the Quran (6:92), the House in Makkah (3:96) and the olive tree (24:35).

primaryMeaning: Three. Thulth is a third, and thālith is the third.
extendedMeaning: The people of the Cave stayed 'three hundred (thalātha mi'atin) years, and added nine' (18:25). The Prophet stood in prayer 'nearly two-thirds of the night, and half of it, and a third of it' (73:20).
quranUsage: Occurs 32 times. The waiting period of divorced women is 'three (thalāthata) menstrual cycles' (2:228). The Quran rejects the Trinity: 'Do not say "Three (thalāthatun)"; desist' (4:171), and 'they have disbelieved who say Allah is the third of three (thālithu thalāthatin)' (5:73). Thulth, 'a third', appears in the inheritance shares (4:11).

primaryMeaning: To resist and refuse to comply — to disobey. Maʿṣiya is disobedience, and ʿāṣī is one who disobeys.
extendedMeaning: Yahya was 'not a tyrant, nor disobedient (ʿaṣiyyā)' (19:14). The secret talk of hypocrites is of 'sin, aggression and disobedience (maʿṣiyat) to the Messenger' (58:8).
quranUsage: Occurs 32 times. 'Adam disobeyed (ʿaṣā) his Lord and erred' (20:121). The Israelites said, 'We hear and disobey (ʿaṣaynā)' (2:93). 'Whoever disobeys (yaʿṣi) Allah and His Messenger … will have a humiliating punishment' (4:14).

primaryMeaning: To stretch and extend — to lengthen something or add to it continuously. Madd is extension; madad and imdād are supply and reinforcement.
extendedMeaning: 'Do not extend (lā tamuddanna) your eyes towards what We have given some of them to enjoy' (15:88). The sea as ink, 'even if We brought the like of it as a supply (madadan)' (18:109).
quranUsage: Occurs 32 times. 'He spread out (madda) the earth' (13:3). Allah reinforces the believers: 'Is it not enough for you that your Lord reinforces you (yumiddakum) with three thousand angels?' (3:124). Allah 'extends (yamudduhum)' the wrongdoers in their transgression (2:15).

primaryMeaning: To set something up, to raise it upright. Naṣb is setting up; nuṣub are stones set up for worship; naṣīb is one's appointed share; naṣab is toil — standing up to hard work.
extendedMeaning: 'When you are free, stand up (fa-nṣab) to worship' (94:7). 'Do not forget your share (naṣībaka) of the world' (28:77).
quranUsage: Occurs 32 times, mostly as naṣīb, 'a share': 'for them is a share (naṣībun) of what they earned' (2:202). Al-anṣāb, 'stone altars', are 'defilement from the work of Satan' (5:90). Naṣab, 'fatigue', is borne in Allah's way and rewarded (9:120).

primaryMeaning: To hide something behind something else. Warā', 'behind', is what is hidden from view; it can mean what is past or what lies ahead, since both are out of sight. Wārā is to cover or conceal.
extendedMeaning: 'Before him (min warā'ihi) is Hell' (14:16). Ishaq was promised, 'and after (warā'i) Ishaq, Yaʿqub' (11:71).
quranUsage: Occurs 32 times, mostly as warā'. Throwing the Book 'behind (warā'a) their backs' means ignoring it (2:101). Warā'ihim, 'before them', means what lies ahead: 'behind them is a barrier until the Day they are raised' (23:100). The crow showed Qabil 'how to hide (yuwārī) the body of his brother' (5:31).

primaryMeaning: To be wide and roomy — the opposite of narrowness. Saʿa is abundance and capacity; wusʿ is what one is able to bear; al-Wāsiʿ is the All-Encompassing.
extendedMeaning: 'My earth is spacious (wāsiʿatun), so worship Me' (29:56). 'Your Lord is vast (wāsiʿu) in forgiveness' (53:32).
quranUsage: Occurs 32 times. 'Allah is All-Encompassing (wāsiʿun), All-Knowing' (2:115). 'His Throne extends over (wasiʿa) the heavens and the earth' (2:255). 'Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity (wusʿahā)' (2:286).

primaryMeaning: To join and connect — to link one's instruction to another's action. Waṣṣā is to enjoin or charge someone with something; waṣiyya is a will or a solemn instruction.
extendedMeaning: Believers 'enjoin one another (tawāṣaw) to truth and enjoin one another to patience' (103:3), and 'to mercy' (90:17).
quranUsage: Occurs 32 times. Allah's commands: 'This He has enjoined on you (waṣṣākum), that you may reason' (6:151), and 'We have enjoined (waṣṣaynā) on man goodness to his parents' (29:8). Waṣiyya, 'a bequest', precedes inheritance: 'after any bequest (waṣiyyatin) he made or debt' (4:11).

primaryMeaning: To appear, to become plain. Badā is to show itself; abdā is to reveal. Bādiya, 'the open desert', is where everything is in plain view.
extendedMeaning: Women are told 'not to display (yubdīna) their adornment' except to those named (24:31). Yusuf spoke of his family coming 'from the desert (al-badw)' (12:100).
quranUsage: Occurs 31 times. On the Day of Judgment 'there will appear (badā) to them from Allah what they had not expected' (39:47). 'If you disclose (tubdū) your charities, it is good' (2:271). Allah knows 'what you reveal (tubdūna) and what you conceal' (2:33).

primaryMeaning: To be free, clear of something — free of a debt, a disease or blame. Al-Bāri' is the Creator who brings creation into being free of imperfection; bariyya is creation.
extendedMeaning: ʿĪsā healed 'the blind and the leper' — ubri'u, 'I heal', making them free of disease (3:49). The believers who do good 'are the best of creation (al-bariyya)' (98:7).
quranUsage: Occurs 31 times. Barī', 'free of', declares a break: 'I am free (barī'un) of what you associate' (6:19), and barā'a, 'a declaration of disassociation', opens Surah 9 (9:1). Al-Bāri', 'the Maker', is a name of Allah (59:24), and Musa called his people to repent 'to your Maker (bāri'ikum)' (2:54).

primaryMeaning: Ḥaythu means 'where' or 'wherever' — a word of place.
extendedMeaning: 'He will provide for him from where (min ḥaythu) he does not expect' (65:3).
quranUsage: Occurs 31 times. Adam and his wife were told, 'eat from it wherever (ḥaythu) you will' (2:35). 'Wherever (ḥaythu) you are, turn your faces towards it' — the Sacred Mosque (2:144). 'Allah knows best where (ḥaythu) to place His message' (6:124).

primaryMeaning: To be pure, clear of any mixture. Akhlaṣa is to make something pure for someone alone; ikhlāṣ is sincerity — doing a thing for Allah alone. Mukhlaṣ is one whom Allah has purified and chosen.
extendedMeaning: 'Is not pure (al-khāliṣ) religion for Allah alone?' (39:3). Musa was 'chosen (mukhlaṣan)' (19:51).
quranUsage: Occurs 31 times. 'Worship Allah, making the religion sincerely (mukhliṣan) His' (39:2). Satan cannot mislead 'Your chosen servants (al-mukhlaṣīn)' (15:40), among them Yusuf (12:24). Surah 112 is named Al-Ikhlāṣ, 'Sincerity'.

primaryMeaning: Evil, harm, wickedness — the opposite of khayr, 'good'. Sharar is a spark that flies out and burns.
extendedMeaning: The slander against ʿĀ'isha was not 'bad (sharran) for you; rather it is good for you' (24:11). Sharar, 'sparks', are thrown from Hell 'as huge as castles' (77:32).
quranUsage: Occurs 31 times. 'Perhaps you dislike a thing and it is good for you; and perhaps you love a thing and it is bad (sharrun) for you' (2:216). The last surahs seek refuge 'from the evil (sharri) of what He created' (113:2). 'The worst (sharra) of creatures with Allah are the deaf and dumb who do not reason' (8:22).

primaryMeaning: To pair — to add one to another so that it becomes two. Shafʿ is an even number; shafāʿa, 'intercession', is joining one's plea to another's to support them.
extendedMeaning: 'By the even (wal-shafʿ) and the odd' (89:3). 'Whoever intercedes (yashfaʿ) for a good cause will have a share of it' (4:85).
quranUsage: Occurs 31 times. On the Day of Judgment 'no intercession (shafāʿatun) will be accepted from it' (2:48), and 'who can intercede (yashfaʿu) with Him except by His permission?' (2:255). 'Intercession (al-shafāʿa) will not benefit except for whom the Most Merciful permits' (20:109).

primaryMeaning: To be clean and pure — the opposite of najas, 'impurity'. Ṭahāra is purity of body and of heart; ṭahhara is to purify; muṭahhar is purified.
extendedMeaning: The spouses of Paradise are 'purified (muṭahhara)' (2:25). Lut's people mocked the believers as 'people who keep themselves pure (yataṭahharūn)' (7:82). 'None touch it except the purified (al-muṭahharūn)' (56:79).
quranUsage: Occurs 31 times. Allah wants 'to purify you (li-yuṭahhirakum)' through ablution (5:6), and 'loves those who purify themselves (al-mutaṭahhirīn)' (2:222). Ibrahim and Ismail were told, 'purify (ṭahhirā) My House' (2:125). Rain is 'pure water (mā'an ṭahūrā)' (25:48).

primaryMeaning: To overcome, to get the upper hand. Ghalaba is to defeat; ghālib is victorious.
extendedMeaning: Surah 30 opens, 'The Romans have been defeated (ghulibat) … but after their defeat they will overcome (sa-yaghlibūn)' (30:2–3). 'Allah is predominant (ghālibun) over His affair' (12:21).
quranUsage: Occurs 31 times. 'The party of Allah — they are the victorious (al-ghālibūn)' (5:56). 'How many a small group has overcome (ghalabat) a large group by Allah's permission' (2:249). 'If Allah helps you, none can overcome (ghāliba) you' (3:160).

primaryMeaning: To sit down, and to stay behind, remaining in place. Maqʿad is a seat or position; qawāʿid are foundations — what a structure sits on.
extendedMeaning: Ibrahim and Ismail 'raised the foundations (al-qawāʿid) of the House' (2:127). The Prophet placed the believers 'in positions (maqāʿida) for battle' (3:121).
quranUsage: Occurs 31 times. Believers remember Allah 'standing, sitting (quʿūdan) and on their sides' (3:191). Those who strive are not equal to 'those who sit (al-qāʿidīn)' at home (4:95). 'Do not sit (lā taqʿudū) with them' while they mock Allah's verses (4:140).

primaryMeaning: To stay, to remain somewhere for a while.
quranUsage: Occurs 31 times, often about how long someone stayed, and how short it seems: 'you will think you had remained (labithtum) only a little' (17:52). The man raised after a hundred years said, 'I have remained (labithtu) a day or part of a day' (2:259). The people of the Cave asked one another how long they had stayed (18:19).

primaryMeaning: To leave, to break off from something or someone. Hijra is leaving one's land for another — emigration; hajr is abandoning; muhājir is an emigrant.
extendedMeaning: 'Leave (fa-hjur) all impurity' (74:5). The Messenger will say, 'My people took this Quran as something abandoned (mahjūrā)' (25:30).
quranUsage: Occurs 31 times. 'Those who believed, emigrated (hājarū) and strove in the way of Allah — they hope for Allah's mercy' (2:218). Al-muhājirūn, 'the emigrants', and the Ansar are praised together (9:100). 'Whoever emigrates (yuhājir) in the way of Allah will find on earth many places of refuge' (4:100).

primaryMeaning: To turn something from its true direction, to overturn it. Ifk is a lie that turns the truth on its head; affāk is a habitual liar; al-mu'tafikāt are 'the overturned cities'.
extendedMeaning: Musa's staff 'swallowed what they falsified (ya'fikūn)' (7:117). Devils come down 'upon every sinful liar (affākin)' (26:222). Al-mu'tafikāt are the cities of Lut's people (69:9).
quranUsage: Occurs 30 times. Anna yu'fakūn, 'how are they turned away (from the truth)?', expresses wonder (5:75). Al-ifk, 'the slander', refers to the false accusation against ʿĀ'isha: 'those who came with the slander (bil-ifk) are a group among you' (24:11).

primaryMeaning: Female — softness and gentleness, the opposite of dhakar, 'male'. Unthā is a female; ināth are females.
extendedMeaning: 'Whoever does righteousness, male or female (unthā), while a believer — We will give them a good life' (16:97).
quranUsage: Occurs 30 times. 'We created you from a male and a female (unthā)' (49:13). Maryam's mother said, 'My Lord, I have delivered a female (unthā) … and the male is not like the female' (3:36). The Quran condemns calling angels or idols female (ināthan) (4:117; 53:21).

extendedMeaning: Striving, walking with purpose, and effort.
quranUsage: 'Man has only what he strives (sa'a) for.' Sa'y between Safa and Marwa.
notes: Sa'y in Hajj commemorates Hajar's search for water.

extendedMeaning: Turning away, diverting, or spending/using something.
quranUsage: Sarafa means to turn. 'We turn away (nasrifu) the ayat.' Tasrif is directing/explaining repeatedly.
notes: Sarf also means morphology - changing word forms.

extendedMeaning: Expressing possibility or hope. Also hardness or difficulty.
quranUsage: 'Asa (عسى) means 'perhaps/maybe.' ''Asa that you dislike something and it is good for you.'
notes: When Allah says 'asa,' it indicates certainty of occurrence.

quranUsage: 'In retaliation (qisas) there is life.' Qisas is retaliation. Qissah is story.
notes: Qisas ensures justice and deters crime.

primaryMeaning: to be Jewish, to repent, guide
extendedMeaning: Being Jewish, or returning/repenting to Allah.
quranUsage: Yahud (يهود) are Jews. Hud is a prophet's name. 'We have repented (hudna) to You.'
notes: Prophet Hud was sent to the people of 'Ad.

quranUsage: 'Seven of the oft-repeated (mathani).' Ithnan is two. Mathani is repeated.
notes: Al-Fatiha is called 'Sab' al-Mathani' (Seven Oft-Repeated).

quranUsage: Jidal (جدال) is argumentation. 'Argue (jadilhum) with them in the best way.' Mujadalah is debate.
notes: Arguing with good manners is permitted for dawah.

quranUsage: 'None knows the soldiers (junud) of your Lord except Him.' Jund is army. Junud is soldiers.
notes: Allah's armies include angels and forces of nature.

quranUsage: 'What will make you know (yudrika)?' Dirayah is knowledge. Idrak is perception.
notes: Full perception of some matters is beyond humans.

quranUsage: 'We raised (rafa'na) him to a high station.' Raf' is raising. Rafi' is high.
notes: 'Isa was raised to Allah. Good deeds raise one's rank.

extendedMeaning: Becoming something, ending up somewhere, final destination.
quranUsage: Sara/yasiru means to become. Masir (مصير) is destination/fate. 'To Allah is the masir (final return).'
notes: Everyone's masir is ultimately to Allah.

extendedMeaning: Birds and flying. Also omens (Arabs read omens from bird flight).
quranUsage: Tayr (bird) appears often. Sulaiman spoke to birds. 'Their fate (ta'ir) is with Allah' - their omen/destiny.
notes: Tatayyur (seeking omens) is prohibited in Islam.

quranUsage: Ghashiya means to cover/overwhelm. 'Al-Ghashiyah' is the Overwhelming (Day of Judgment). Ghishawah is a covering.
notes: Surah Al-Ghashiyah describes the overwhelming Day.

quranUsage: 'That is the great success (fawz).' Fawz is success. Fa'iz is successful.
notes: True success is entering Paradise.

extendedMeaning: Loving affection and friendship. Desire for closeness.
quranUsage: Al-Wadud (The Loving) is one of Allah's names. 'My Lord is merciful and loving (wadud).'
notes: Mawaddah is the deep affection between spouses.

extendedMeaning: Endless time stretching into the future. Permanence without end.
quranUsage: Abadan means forever. 'Dwelling therein forever (abadan)' describes Paradise and Hell.
notes: Abad is future eternity, azal is past eternity.

extendedMeaning: Heaviness, weight, and burden. Also valuable (weighty) things.
quranUsage: Thaqil is heavy. 'Heavy (thaqil) word.' Thaqalan are jinn and humans.
notes: The Quran is described as a 'heavy word' - weighty in meaning.

quranUsage: 'Purify your garments (thiyab).' Thawb is garment. Thawab is reward.
notes: Thawab (reward) is what 'returns' to you for good deeds.

quranUsage: Ahata means to encompass. 'Allah encompasses (muhit) all things.' Muhit is surrounding.
notes: Allah's knowledge encompasses everything.

primaryMeaning: to be empty, alone, pass away
extendedMeaning: Being empty, alone, or past generations that have passed.
quranUsage: Khala means to pass/be alone. 'Nations that have passed (khalat) before.' Khalwah is seclusion.
notes: Past nations serve as warnings for current ones.

extendedMeaning: Expectation of something good. Hope that motivates action.
quranUsage: Raja' (hope) in Allah's mercy is essential. 'Whoever hopes to meet his Lord, let him do righteous deeds.'
notes: Hope without action is mere wishful thinking (umniyyah).

quranUsage: 'Seven (sab') heavens.' Sab'ah is seven. Sab' also means wild beast.
notes: Seven heavens, seven earths, seven circuits of tawaf.

quranUsage: 'We split (shaqaqna) the earth.' Shaqq is splitting. Shiqaq is discord.
notes: Allah splits the earth for plants to grow.

extendedMeaning: Giving everything its due right. Perfect balance and equity.
quranUsage: Allah commands 'adl (justice). It appears alongside ihsan (excellence) in the famous verse of Surah An-Nahl.
notes: Justice even toward enemies is commanded: 'Let not hatred prevent you from being just.'

extendedMeaning: Growing, originating, or bringing something into existence.
quranUsage: Ansha'a means to originate/create. 'We originated (ansha'na) them as a creation.' Nash'ah is growth.
notes: Al-Munshi' is one who originates creation.

extendedMeaning: Absolute certainty that removes all doubt. The highest level of knowledge.
quranUsage: Yaqeen is certainty. 'Worship your Lord until certainty (yaqeen) comes to you.' Three levels: 'ilm, 'ayn, haqq al-yaqeen.
notes: Yaqeen often refers to death - the certainty that comes to all.

quranUsage: 'Enter through the gate (bab) prostrating.' Bab is door/gate.
notes: Paradise has eight gates; Hell has seven.

quranUsage: 'Travel (siru) through the earth.' Sayr is travel. Sirah is biography.
notes: Traveling to reflect on past nations is encouraged.

extendedMeaning: Trees (with intertwining branches), and disputation (ideas intertwining).
quranUsage: 'Have you seen what you sow? Is it you who makes it grow or are We the grower?' Shajar is tree. Shajara is dispute.
notes: The forbidden tree in Paradise and the tree of Zaqqum in Hell.

quranUsage: 'Do you wonder ('ajibta)?' 'Ajab is wonder. 'Ujb is vanity.
notes: Wondering at Allah's signs leads to faith; self-admiration leads to arrogance.

quranUsage: 'Warn your closest clan ('ashirah).' 'Ashirah is clan. Mu'asharah is companionship.
notes: The Prophet first warned his closest relatives.

extendedMeaning: Deception, delusion, and being fooled by appearances.
quranUsage: 'Let not the worldly life delude (yaghurrannaka) you.' Ghurur is delusion.
notes: The world (dunya) is described as deceptive enjoyment.

extendedMeaning: The moon as the night luminary and time marker.
quranUsage: Al-Qamar (The Moon) is Surah 54. The moon split as a miracle. It marks months and seasons.
notes: The Islamic calendar is lunar (qamari).

extendedMeaning: City or urban settlement. Also civilization.
quranUsage: Madinah (مدينة) is city. 'The people of the Madinah.' Al-Madinah refers to the Prophet's city.
notes: Madinah was called Yathrib before the Prophet's migration.

quranUsage: Amsaka means to hold/withhold. 'Hold (amsik) your wife.' Mustamsik is one who holds firmly.
notes: Holding firmly to the Quran is commanded.

extendedMeaning: Bestowing favor, and reminding of favors (negatively).
quranUsage: 'Allah has bestowed favor (manna) upon the believers.' Mann is favor.
notes: Allah's mann is blessing; human mann (reminding of favors) is discouraged.

quranUsage: 'Appoint for me a minister (wazir) from my family.' Wazir is minister. Wizr is burden/sin.
notes: Harun was Musa's wazir. Everyone carries their own wizr (burden of sin).

extendedMeaning: Intensely blazing fire, one of the names of Hell.
quranUsage: Jahim (جحيم) is blazing Hellfire. 'Surely the Jahim is lying in wait.' One of Hell's names.
notes: Jahim describes the intense blazing of Hell's fire.

quranUsage: Khizyi (خزي) is disgrace. 'They will have disgrace (khizy) in this world.' Akhza is to disgrace.
notes: Disbelievers face khizy in both worlds.

extendedMeaning: Being unable, incapacity, and the weakness of old age.
quranUsage: 'You cannot escape (mu'jizin) in the earth.' 'Ajuz is old woman. I'jaz is miraculous inimitability.
notes: The Quran's i'jaz (inimitability) proves human inability to match it.

quranUsage: 'We cause to grow (nunbitu) gardens.' Nabat is plant. 'A good growth (nabatan hasanan).'
notes: Maryam was raised with 'good growth' by Zakariyya.

extendedMeaning: Being easy or light. Also humiliation and disgrace.
quranUsage: Hawn is ease/humiliation. 'Walk with humility (hawnan).' Muhaanat is contempt.
notes: Walking with hawn means calmly, without arrogance.

extendedMeaning: Placing down, lowering, and giving birth.
quranUsage: 'She placed (wada'at) him.' Wad' is placing. Mawdu' is placed/topic.
notes: Can mean giving birth or putting something down.

extendedMeaning: Adam (first human), skin, or brownish color.
quranUsage: Adam (آدم) is the first human. 'We created Adam.' Adim is skin/surface.
notes: Adam is called so possibly due to his brown earth origin.

quranUsage: 'Allah expands (yabsutu) provision.' Bast is expansion. Basit is extended.
notes: Allah contracts and expands provision as He wills.

extendedMeaning: Belly/stomach, interior, and the hidden aspect of things.
quranUsage: 'The outer (zahir) and the inner (batin).' Batn is belly. Batin is inner/hidden.
notes: Al-Batin (The Hidden) is one of Allah's names - His essence is beyond comprehension.

quranUsage: Al-Hadid (Iron) is Surah 57. 'We sent down iron (hadid).' Hudud are Allah's limits.
notes: Iron was sent down as a blessing with great benefits.

extendedMeaning: Being present, attending, and settling (in cities).
quranUsage: 'When death approaches (hadara) one of you.' Hudur is presence. Hadir is present.
notes: Hadari (settled) vs. Badawi (bedouin) - urban vs. desert.

quranUsage: 'Two complete years (hawlayn)' for breastfeeding. Hawla means around.
notes: Hawl is a complete year cycle.

quranUsage: 'We gave you drink (asqaynakum).' Saqy is giving drink. Saqi is cupbearer.
notes: Allah provides drink from clouds and springs.

quranUsage: 'They sold (sharaw) him for a small price.' Shira' is buying. Ishtara is to purchase.
notes: Yusuf was sold for a few coins.

quranUsage: 'They will burn (yaslaw) in the Fire.' Salla is to burn. Saly is roasting.
notes: Different from ص-ل-و (prayer) - this relates to fire.

extendedMeaning: Orbit, sphere, and ship (which orbits the water).
quranUsage: 'Each in an orbit (falak) swimming.' Falak is orbit/sphere.
notes: Celestial bodies swim in their orbits - Quranic precision.

quranUsage: 'Allah loves those who are equitable (muqsitin).' Qist is equity.
notes: Al-Muqsit (The Equitable) is Allah's name.

extendedMeaning: Tongue as organ of speech and language itself.
quranUsage: Lisan is tongue/language. 'We sent every messenger in the language (lisan) of his people.'
notes: Lisan al-'Arab is the Arabic language.

quranUsage: Wa'z (وعظ) is admonition. 'Admonish (i'z) them.' Maw'izah is good advice/sermon.
notes: The Quran is called a maw'izah for mankind.

extendedMeaning: Granting or bestowing something as a gift without exchange.
quranUsage: Al-Wahhab (الوهاب) is the Bestower - Allah's name. 'Grant us (hab lana) from You mercy.' Hibah is gift.
notes: Allah grants without expecting anything in return.

extendedMeaning: Causing harm, hurt, or annoyance to others.
quranUsage: Adha is harm/annoyance. 'Do not harm (tu'dhu) the Prophet.' Idha'ah is causing harm.
notes: Harming believers and the Prophet is severely warned against.

extendedMeaning: Fruit and the result or product of something.
quranUsage: 'Eat of His fruit (thamarihi) when it ripens.' Thamar is fruit. Thamara is to bear fruit.
notes: Paradise has fruits of every kind.

extendedMeaning: Not just lack of knowledge but actively ignoring truth. Jahiliyyah is the 'age of ignorance'.
quranUsage: Jahl is the opposite of 'ilm (knowledge). The pre-Islamic era is called Jahiliyyah.
notes: True ignorance is not lack of information but denial of evident truth.

extendedMeaning: Humility, being low, or being made easy and manageable.
quranUsage: Dhull (ذل) is humility/lowliness. 'Lower (dhull) your wing to believers.' Mudhalal is made easy.
notes: Dhull before Allah is praiseworthy; before others is blame.

extendedMeaning: Watching, observing. Also neck, and by extension, freeing slaves.
quranUsage: Raqib (رقيب) is the Watchful - Allah's name. Raqabah is freeing a slave (neck). 'Allah is Raqib over you.'
notes: Freeing raqabah (slave) is expiation for sins.

extendedMeaning: Life span, visiting (Umrah), and populating/building up.
quranUsage: 'Complete the Hajj and Umrah for Allah.' 'Umr is life. 'Umrah is lesser pilgrimage.
notes: Umrah is the lesser pilgrimage that can be performed anytime.

extendedMeaning: Strong displeasure. Divine anger is just, human anger should be controlled.
quranUsage: 'Not those who earned Your anger (ghadab)' in Al-Fatihah. Allah's wrath is upon persistent sinners.
notes: The Prophet advised: 'Do not be angry' repeatedly.

extendedMeaning: Dawn breaking forth. Also wickedness (breaking moral bounds).
quranUsage: Al-Fajr (The Dawn) is Surah 89. Fajr prayer time. Fujur is wickedness/immorality.
notes: The contrast: dawn is pure, fujur is moral corruption.

extendedMeaning: Going to excess in evil, particularly in matters of modesty and decency.
quranUsage: Fahishah (pl. fawahish) refers to major sins, especially sexual immorality. The Quran forbids even approaching fahishah.

extendedMeaning: Being on the verge of, almost doing something.
quranUsage: Kada/yakadu means 'almost.' 'They almost (yakadu) cannot see.' Related to ك-ي-د.

extendedMeaning: Physical illness or spiritual disease (doubt, hypocrisy).
quranUsage: Marad is sickness. 'In their hearts is disease (marad).' Marid is sick person.
notes: Heart disease refers to spiritual ailments like doubt and hypocrisy.

quranUsage: Waqa'a means to occur/fall. 'When the Event (waqi'ah) occurs.' Waqi' is happening/reality.
notes: Al-Waqi'ah (The Event) is a name for Day of Judgment.

quranUsage: 'Race (sari'u) to forgiveness.' Sur'ah is speed. Musri' is speeding.
notes: We should hasten to good deeds.

extendedMeaning: Exceeding proper limits, extravagance, and wastefulness.
quranUsage: Israf (إسراف) is extravagance. 'Do not be extravagant (musrifin).' Musrif is wasteful person.
notes: Allah does not love the musrifin (wasteful).

quranUsage: 'Divorce (talaq) is twice.' Talaq is divorce. Itlaq is release.
notes: Divorce has specific rules in Islam.

quranUsage: 'We drowned (aghraqna) those who denied.' Gharaq is drowning.
notes: Drowning was the fate of Firawn and denying nations.

extendedMeaning: Wearing clothes, garments. Also mixing/confusing (covering truth).
quranUsage: Libas is clothing. 'Clothing (libas) of taqwa is best.' 'Do not mix (talbisu) truth with falsehood.'
notes: Spouses are described as 'clothing' for each other.

extendedMeaning: Walking and movement by foot. Proceeding through life.
quranUsage: 'Walk (imshi) in the earth and eat of His provision.' Mashsha'un are those who walk.
notes: Walking humbly is praised; walking arrogantly condemned.

extendedMeaning: Marriage contract and the marital relationship.
quranUsage: 'Marry (ankihu) those among you who are single.' Nikah is marriage.
notes: Marriage is described as half of faith.

quranUsage: 'Give full measure and weigh (zinu) with justice.' Mizan is scale/balance.
notes: The scales (mawazin) will weigh deeds on Judgment Day.

extendedMeaning: Orphan (one who lost their father), and being alone.
quranUsage: 'Did He not find you (O Muhammad) an orphan (yatim) and give refuge?' Yatim is orphan.
notes: Caring for orphans is heavily emphasized in Islam.

quranUsage: 'A thousand (alf) years.' Alf is thousand. Ulfah is familiarity.
notes: Laylat al-Qadr is better than a thousand months.

extendedMeaning: Dust, soil - the material of human creation.
quranUsage: 'We created you from dust (turab).' Turab is soil/dust.
notes: Humans were created from dust and return to it.

quranUsage: 'Today I have completed (atmamtu) for you your religion.' Tamam is completion.
notes: Islam was completed during the Prophet's final pilgrimage.

extendedMeaning: Making a mistake, erring, or sinning.
quranUsage: Khata' (خطأ) is mistake/sin. Khati'ah is a sin. 'Do not kill your children - that is a great khit' (sin).'
notes: Khata' can be unintentional; khatee'ah is more deliberate.

extendedMeaning: Four, springtime, and a square/dwelling place.
quranUsage: 'Four (arba'ah) months.' Arba'ah is four. Rabi' is spring.
notes: Four sacred months, four witnesses for certain cases.

extendedMeaning: Arab people, Arabic language, or being clear and eloquent.
quranUsage: Arabi (عربي) means Arabic. 'A Quran in Arabic (Arabiyyan).' A'rab are Bedouin Arabs.
notes: Arabic was chosen for the Quran's clear expression.

quranUsage: 'By Your might, I will mislead (la-ughwiyannahum) them.' Ghawayah is deviation.
notes: Satan vowed to mislead humanity.

extendedMeaning: Happiness and rejoicing. Can be praiseworthy or blameworthy depending on its cause.
quranUsage: Rejoicing in Allah's bounty is good. Excessive pride (farah) in worldly things is criticized.
notes: Qarun's arrogant rejoicing led to his destruction.

quranUsage: Taman means to wish. Umniyah is wish/desire. Maniy is sperm. 'From a drop of maniy (sperm) emitted.'
notes: Amaniy (wishes) without action lead nowhere.

extendedMeaning: A trace, mark, or effect. Also preferring something.
quranUsage: Athar (أثر) is trace/effect. 'Follow the traces (athar) of Allah's mercy.' Ithaar is preferring others.
notes: The Ansar showed ithaar (preferring others over themselves).

quranUsage: 'What remains (yabqa) with Allah is better.' Al-Baqi is The Everlasting.
notes: Only Allah is truly everlasting (Al-Baqi).

extendedMeaning: Stone, and the concept of being blocked/forbidden. Hijr is also lap/protection.
quranUsage: Hajar is stone. Hijr can mean forbidden sanctuary. 'Stones (hijarah) prepared for disbelievers.'
notes: Al-Hajar al-Aswad is the Black Stone of the Ka'bah.

extendedMeaning: Being cautious, taking precautions, and guarding against.
quranUsage: Hadhira means to beware. 'Beware (uhdhar) of them.' Hidhr is caution.
notes: Taking precautions is wisdom, not lack of trust.

extendedMeaning: Self-restraint despite having power. Also dreams and maturity.
quranUsage: Al-Halim (The Forbearing) is Allah's name. Ibrahim was described as halim (forbearing).
notes: Hilm is restraining anger when one has power to act on it.

quranUsage: Hamamah is dove/pigeon. Hamim is hot water.
notes: Doves nested at the cave during the Hijrah.

extendedMeaning: Established way, practice, and natural law. Sunnah is the Prophet's practice.
quranUsage: 'The practice (sunnah) of those who were sent before.' Sunnah is established way.
notes: Allah's sunnah (way) in dealing with nations does not change.

extendedMeaning: Month (lunar cycle) and making something famous/known.
quranUsage: 'The month (shahr) of Ramadan.' Mashhur is famous/well-known.
notes: Months are determined by moon phases.

primaryMeaning: youth, young man, to give ruling
extendedMeaning: Youth, young man, or giving a legal ruling (fatwa).
quranUsage: Fata (فتى) is young man. 'The youths (fityah) believed.' Fatwa is legal ruling. Mufti gives fatwa.
notes: The people of the cave were youths who believed.

quranUsage: Katama means to conceal. 'Do not conceal (taktumu) testimony.' Kitman is concealment.
notes: Concealing knowledge is condemned.

quranUsage: 'He spreads (yanshuru) His mercy.' Nashr is spreading. Nushur is resurrection.
notes: Allah spreads His mercy and will spread the dead in resurrection.

quranUsage: 'The party (hizb) of Allah.' Hizb is party. Ahzab are factions.
notes: The party of Allah will be successful.

quranUsage: Darajah (درجة) is degree/rank. 'They have degrees (darajat) with Allah.' Tadarruj is gradual progression.
notes: People have different darajat based on their deeds.

extendedMeaning: Growth and increase. Riba (usury) is illegitimate increase.
quranUsage: Riba (usury) is strictly forbidden. 'Allah destroys riba and increases charity.'
notes: Riba literally means 'increase' but refers to prohibited interest.

extendedMeaning: Year, or a long period of time.
quranUsage: Sanah (سنة) is year. Sinin is years. 'We punished them with years (sinin) of famine.'
notes: Sanah is year; 'am is also year but more general.

extendedMeaning: Making things with skill and craftsmanship.
quranUsage: 'The making (sun') of Allah who perfected everything.' Sina'ah is craft/industry.
notes: Allah is the best of makers.

primaryMeaning: to create, originate, break fast, natural disposition
extendedMeaning: Original creation, splitting/breaking open, and natural state.
quranUsage: Fatir is Originator (Surah 35). Fitrah is natural disposition. Iftar is breaking fast.
notes: Every child is born upon fitrah (natural inclination to truth).

extendedMeaning: Deep understanding, especially of religion. Fiqh became the term for Islamic jurisprudence.
quranUsage: 'That they may understand (yafqahun).' Fiqh is deep understanding. Faqih is jurist.
notes: Fiqh goes beyond mere knowledge ('ilm) to penetrating understanding.

quranUsage: 'He removes (yakshifu) the hardship.' Kashf is uncovering. Inkishaf is revelation.
notes: Only Allah can truly remove hardship.

extendedMeaning: Playing, sporting, or treating something as a jest.
quranUsage: La'ib is play/sport. 'This worldly life is but play (la'ib) and amusement.' La'ib contrasts with serious matters.
notes: Life should not be taken merely as play.

extendedMeaning: Doubt, disputation, or passing by something.
quranUsage: Miryah (مرية) is doubt. 'Do not be in doubt (miryah) about it.' Marra means to pass by.
notes: No miryah should exist about meeting Allah.

extendedMeaning: Date palm tree - symbol of blessing and provision.
quranUsage: 'Shake the trunk of the palm tree (nakhlah)' - to Maryam. Nakhil is palm trees.
notes: Palm trees are frequently mentioned as signs of blessing.

quranUsage: 'He removed (naza'a) from them their clothing.' Naz' is removing.
notes: Satan stripped Adam and Hawwa of Paradise clothing.

quranUsage: 'We breathed (nafakhna) into him of Our spirit.' Nafkh is blowing.
notes: Allah breathed His spirit into Adam.

quranUsage: Balad (بلد) is country/town. 'This is a secure balad (town).' Bilad is countries.
notes: Al-Balad is Surah 90, referring to Makkah.

quranUsage: 'One-eighth (thumun).' Thumun is one-eighth. Thaman is price.
notes: Wives inherit one-eighth when there are children.

extendedMeaning: Right guidance, maturity, and proper conduct.
quranUsage: 'Perhaps my Lord will guide me to right conduct (rushd).' Rushd is right guidance.
notes: Ar-Rashid (The Guide to Right Path) is Allah's name.

extendedMeaning: Blazing fire, one of the names of Hell. Also price.
quranUsage: Sa'ir (سعير) is blazing fire - a name of Hell. 'They will be in the Sa'ir.' Su'r is price/rate.
notes: Sa'ir emphasizes the blazing intensity of Hell.

extendedMeaning: Form, image, shape, and the act of forming.
quranUsage: Al-Musawwir (The Fashioner) is Allah's name. 'He forms (yusawwiru) you in the wombs.' Surah is chapter (a form).
notes: Allah shapes each person uniquely in the womb.

quranUsage: 'When the sun rises (tala'at).' Tulu' is rising. Ittala'a is to learn/discover.
notes: The sun's rising is a daily sign.

extendedMeaning: West direction, sunset, and being strange/foreign.
quranUsage: 'Lord of the East and West (maghrib).' Gharb is west. Gharib is stranger.
notes: Islam began as something strange and will return to being strange.

extendedMeaning: Fruit, or enjoying and delighting in something.
quranUsage: Fakihah (فاكهة) is fruit. 'Fruits (fawakihu) of what they desire.' Fakihin is enjoying.
notes: Paradise has abundant fruits.

quranUsage: 'Allah keeps firm (yuthabbitu) those who believe.' Thabit is firm/stable.
notes: Allah stabilizes believers with firm words.

quranUsage: Husn is fortress. Muhsanah is chaste woman. 'Protected (muhsanat) women.' Hisn is fortress.
notes: Ihsan also relates to fortifying oneself with marriage.

quranUsage: Khasm (خصم) is opponent/disputant. 'Has the story of the disputants (khasim) reached you?'
notes: Referring to angels who visited Prophet Dawud.

extendedMeaning: Any creature that moves on earth (from insect to elephant).
quranUsage: 'There is no creature (dabbah) on earth but that upon Allah is its provision.' Dabbah is creature.
notes: Allah provides for every creature, however small.

extendedMeaning: Head, chief, or top of something.
quranUsage: Ra's (رأس) is head. 'You will have your ra's (principal) of your wealth.' Also top/chief.
notes: Ra's al-mal is principal/capital in finance.

extendedMeaning: Religious obligation, ordaining, and fixed portion.
quranUsage: 'Allah has ordained (farada) for you.' Faridah is obligation. Fard is duty.
notes: Fard is a religious duty that must be performed.

extendedMeaning: Deep thinking and reflection. Mental processing of ideas.
quranUsage: Tafakkur (reflection) is commanded repeatedly. 'Will they not reflect (yatafakkarun)?'
notes: Thinking about Allah's creation leads to faith.

extendedMeaning: Nearness, being at or from someone's presence.
quranUsage: Ladun (لدن) means 'at/from.' 'A mercy from Us (min ladunna).' Indicates direct presence.
notes: 'Ilm ladunni is knowledge directly from Allah.

extendedMeaning: Establishing firmly, enabling, and giving power.
quranUsage: 'We established (makkanna) them on earth.' Tamkin is establishment/empowerment.
notes: Allah establishes believers when they establish His religion.

extendedMeaning: Religion, creed, or way. Also to dictate.
quranUsage: Millah (ملة) is religion/creed. 'The millah (religion) of Ibrahim.' Imlal is dictation.
notes: Millah Ibrahim is the pure monotheistic religion.

extendedMeaning: Fleeing, marching forth, or having aversion.
quranUsage: Nafara means to flee/march. 'March forth (infiru) light or heavy.' Nafar is group of people.
notes: Believers should march forth in Allah's cause.

quranUsage: Anaba means to turn (to Allah). 'Turn (anibu) to your Lord.' Munib is one who turns back.
notes: Related to tawbah but emphasizes returning fully.

quranUsage: Awwab (أواب) is frequently returning. 'Indeed he was awwab (oft-returning).' Describes prophets.
notes: Prophet Dawud and Sulayman were called awwab.

extendedMeaning: Settling in a place, preparing a place, or returning with something.
quranUsage: Tabawwa'a means to settle. 'We settled (bawwa'na) Ibrahim at the House.' Ba'a is to return (often with sin).

extendedMeaning: Deep humility and submission, especially in worship. The stillness of awe.
quranUsage: Khushu' in prayer is praised. The earth becomes 'khashi'ah' (humble/barren) before rain revives it.
notes: Khushu' is the heart's submission that shows in the body's stillness.

extendedMeaning: Being light in weight, easy, or lessening a burden.
quranUsage: 'Allah wishes to lighten (yukhaffif) for you.' Khafif is light/easy.
notes: Islam aims to lighten burdens, not make things difficult.

primaryMeaning: to wait, watch, lie in wait
extendedMeaning: Waiting, watching, or lying in wait.
quranUsage: Tarabbasa means to wait. 'Wait (tarabbasu), indeed we are waiting.' Mutarabbis waits.
notes: Used for both patient waiting and lying in ambush.

extendedMeaning: Claiming, asserting, or thinking something to be true.
quranUsage: Za'ama means to claim. 'They claim (yaz'umun) they believe.' Za'm is claim (often false).
notes: Often used for false or unsubstantiated claims.

extendedMeaning: Wall (surrounding), chapter of Quran, and leaping over.
quranUsage: 'A wall (sur) between them.' Sur is wall. Surah is chapter.
notes: Each surah is like a walled enclosure of meaning.

quranUsage: Saqa means to drive. 'We drive (suqna) it to a dead land.' Saq is leg. Suq is market.
notes: Clouds are 'driven' to bring rain.

quranUsage: 'Lord of the East (mashriq) and West.' Sharq is east. Shurooq is sunrise.
notes: The sun rises from the east - a daily sign.

quranUsage: 'Drink pure (safiya) and pleasant.' Safi is pure. Istifa' is selection.
notes: Allah selects (yastafi) whom He wills for His message.

quranUsage: 'Audhu billah means 'I seek refuge in Allah.' A'udhu is seeking protection. Ma'adh is refuge.
notes: Seeking refuge in Allah is the ultimate protection.

quranUsage: 'What prevented (mana'a) you from prostrating?' Man' is prevention. Mani' is protector.
notes: Al-Mani' - The Preventer - protects from harm.

quranUsage: Intaqama means to take revenge. 'We took vengeance (intaqamna) from them.' Niqmah is retribution.
notes: Allah's punishment is just retribution.

quranUsage: 'Whether you speak aloud (tajhar).' Jahr is speaking aloud.
notes: Allah knows what is spoken aloud and what is hidden.

extendedMeaning: Deeds becoming void, nullified, or in vain.
quranUsage: Habita means to become void. 'Their deeds have become void (habitat).' Ihbat is nullification.
notes: Disbelief nullifies good deeds.

extendedMeaning: What is impure, filthy, or morally corrupt.
quranUsage: Khabith is impure/evil. 'The evil (khabith) and good are not equal.' Khaba'ith are impurities.
notes: Khabith is opposite of tayyib.

quranUsage: 'Do not betray (takhun) Allah and the Messenger.' Khiyanah is betrayal.
notes: Betraying trusts is a sign of hypocrisy.

extendedMeaning: Lines of writing, to write systematically.
quranUsage: 'By the pen and what they write in lines (yasturun).' Asatir are written tales.
notes: Satr is a line of text.

extendedMeaning: Preparing, making ready, or having something prepared.
quranUsage: A'tadna means We have prepared. 'We have prepared ('atadna) for the disbelievers a painful punishment.'

extendedMeaning: Making something public and open, announcement.
quranUsage: 'Whether you reveal (tu'linu) something or conceal it.' 'Alaniyah is openness.
notes: Charity can be given secretly or openly.

extendedMeaning: Morning time, or going out early in the morning.
quranUsage: Ghuduww is morning. 'Glorify Him morning (ghuduwwan) and evening.' Ghada means to go early.
'Shackles (aghlal) on their necks.' Ghull is shackle/yoke.
notes: The Prophet removed the shackles of ignorance.

extendedMeaning: The heart as seat of emotions and intellect.
quranUsage: Fu'ad (فؤاد) is heart. 'The fu'ad (heart) of Musa's mother became empty.' Af'idah is hearts (plural).
notes: Fu'ad emphasizes the emotional aspect of the heart.

quranUsage: 'Give full measure (kayl).' Kayl is measure. Mikyal is measuring vessel.
notes: Giving full measure in trade is commanded.

quranUsage: 'A reminder for those of understanding (uli al-albab).' Lubb is core/intellect.
notes: Uli al-albab are people of deep understanding.

extendedMeaning: Idle amusement, distraction from serious matters.
quranUsage: Lahw (لهو) is amusement/distraction. 'This worldly life is but play and lahw (amusement).'
notes: Lahw distracts from remembrance of Allah.

extendedMeaning: A cradle, bed, or preparing/spreading something.
quranUsage: Mahd (مهد) is cradle/bed. 'Who made the earth a mahd (bed) for you.' Also the cradle of Isa.
Bada'a means to begin. 'As He originated (bada'a) you, so you will return.' Bad' is beginning.

extendedMeaning: Buying and selling. Bay'ah is also pledge of allegiance (a transaction of loyalty).
quranUsage: Bay' is trade. 'Allah has permitted trade (bay') and forbidden usury.' Bay'ah is pledge to a leader.
notes: Honest trade is highly praised.

quranUsage: Haraj (حرج) is difficulty. 'There is no haraj (difficulty) on you.' Also narrow/constricted.
notes: Islam removes haraj (hardship) from people.

extendedMeaning: Being free (not enslaved), heat, or writing. A hurr is a free person.
quranUsage: Tahrir raqabah is freeing a slave. Harr is heat. Huruf are letters (freed/released sounds).
notes: Freedom from slavery is highly encouraged in Islam.

quranUsage: 'You will surely ride (latarkabunna) stage after stage.' Rukub is riding. Markab is vehicle.
notes: Riding is a blessing - from animals to ships.

extendedMeaning: Pasturing animals, or marking/branding. Also inflicting punishment.
quranUsage: Sawwama means to inflict. 'They inflicted (yasumunakum) upon you the worst punishment.'
'If you are in doubt (shakk).' Shakk is doubt.
notes: Doubt in faith is dangerous; seeking knowledge removes doubt.

extendedMeaning: Deafness - inability to hear truth. Also solid/firm.
quranUsage: Samm is deaf. 'Deaf (summ), dumb, blind - they do not return.'
notes: Spiritual deafness means refusing to hear guidance.

quranUsage: 'Restrain (kuffu) your hands.' Kaff is palm. Kaff is to restrain.
notes: The palm is used in greeting and restraint.

quranUsage: 'Wipe (imsahu) over your heads.' Masih is the anointed one (Christ).
notes: Isa is called Al-Masih (the Messiah/Anointed).

extendedMeaning: Rain that brings life. Can also refer to harmful rain (punishment).
quranUsage: Matar is rain. 'We sent down rain (matar)' for life. Punishment also 'rained' on sinful nations.
notes: Rain symbolizes both mercy and punishment in the Quran.

quranUsage: Mathwa (مثوى) is abode. 'Hell is the mathwa (abode) of the arrogant.'
'Whoever desires the harvest (harth) of the Hereafter.' Harth is tillage/harvest.
notes: Life is a field we cultivate for the Hereafter.

extendedMeaning: Stoning, cursing, or speaking based on conjecture.
quranUsage: Rajm is stoning/cursing. 'Accursed (rajim) Satan.' Rajm bil-ghayb is speaking without knowledge.
notes: Shaytan is called 'rajim' (accursed/stoned).

quranUsage: 'And it came to rest (istawat) on Mount Judi.' Rasa is to anchor. Rawasi are mountains (anchors).
notes: Mountains are like anchors for the earth.

quranUsage: 'Is it you who cause it to grow (tazra'unahu) or are We the grower?' Zar' is crops/planting.
notes: Agriculture is presented as a sign of Allah's creative power.

quranUsage: Saff (صف) is row. 'Indeed Allah loves those who fight in rows (saffan).' Saffat are those arranged in rows.
notes: Angels and believers stand in rows.

extendedMeaning: Abstaining from food, drink, and desires. Also means maintaining silence or stillness.
quranUsage: Sawm (fasting) in Ramadan is one of the five pillars. Maryam was commanded to observe a 'fast of silence'.
'Ashiyy (عشي) is evening. 'Glorify Him evening ('ashiyyan) and morning.' 'Isha is nightfall.

extendedMeaning: Giving generously. Allah is the ultimate giver.
quranUsage: 'Your Lord will give you and you will be satisfied.' 'Ata' (gift) from Allah.
notes: Al-Mu'ti (The Giver) is among Allah's names in hadith.

extendedMeaning: Being in need, poverty. All creation is faqir (needy) before Allah.
quranUsage: 'You are the poor (fuqara') unto Allah.' Faqir is poor/needy person.
notes: Spiritual poverty (recognizing need for Allah) is praised.

quranUsage: 'The self-reproaching (lawwamah) soul.' 'Do not fear the blame of blamers.'
notes: An-Nafs al-Lawwamah is the self-blaming soul - sign of conscience.

quranUsage: Wasafa means to describe. 'Glory to Allah above what they describe (yasifun).'
notes: Allah is beyond human descriptions.

quranUsage: Walaja means to enter. 'He knows what enters (yaliju) the earth.' Wuluj is entering.
Aba means to refuse. 'Iblis refused (aba) and was arrogant.' Iba' is refusal.
notes: Iblis's refusal to prostrate was from arrogance.

quranUsage: Baghtatan (بغتة) means suddenly. 'The Hour will come upon them suddenly (baghtatan).'
notes: The Day of Judgment comes suddenly.

quranUsage: 'Their skins (julud) will testify.' Jild is skin. Jalad is endurance.
notes: On Judgment Day, skins will testify against their owners.

quranUsage: 'The neighbor (jar).' Jar is neighbor. Jawr is injustice.
notes: Neighbors have great rights in Islam.

quranUsage: 'They swear (yahlifun) by Allah.' Half is oath. Hilf is alliance.
notes: False oaths are a serious sin.

extendedMeaning: Returning, or intense whiteness. Hur are maidens with beautiful eyes.
quranUsage: Hur (حور) are fair maidens of Paradise. 'Companions with beautiful eyes (hur 'in).' Hiwar is dialogue.
notes: Hur 'in describes the contrast in eye color.

quranUsage: Khazana means to store. Khaza'in are treasures. 'To Allah belong the khaza'in (treasures) of the heavens and earth.'
notes: Khazanah is the keepers of Hell.

quranUsage: 'Allah took Ibrahim as a close friend (khalil).' Khalil is intimate friend.
notes: Ibrahim is Khalilullah - the intimate friend of Allah.

quranUsage: Ra'fah (رأفة) is compassion. 'Rauf' (الرؤوف) is the Compassionate - Allah's name. 'Allah is Ra'uf to the servants.'
notes: Ra'fah is a tender, gentle form of mercy.

extendedMeaning: Bowing, especially in prayer. Also humbling oneself.
quranUsage: 'Bow (irka'u) and prostrate.' Ruku' is bowing. Raki' is one who bows.
notes: Ruku' in prayer symbolizes humility before Allah.

quranUsage: Shahwah (شهوة) is desire. 'Beautified for people is the love of shahawat (desires).' Ishtaha is to desire.
notes: Controlling shahawat is part of self-discipline.

extendedMeaning: Being small, young, and being humiliated.
quranUsage: 'Small (saghir) or great.' Saghir is small. Saghar is humiliation.
notes: No deed is too small to be recorded.

quranUsage: 'A single shout (sayhah) seized them.' Sayhah is shout/blast.
notes: Many nations were destroyed by a single shout.

extendedMeaning: Being narrow, tight, or in distress.
quranUsage: 'Do not be in distress (dayq).' 'The earth became narrow (daqat) for them.'
notes: Spiritual constriction comes from turning away from guidance.

extendedMeaning: Serenity, calmness, and reassurance of the heart.
quranUsage: Itma'naan is tranquility. 'Hearts find rest (tatma'innu) in the remembrance of Allah.' Mutma'innah is tranquil.
notes: The tranquil soul (nafs mutma'innah) returns to Allah.

extendedMeaning: Protection and preservation from harm. 'Ismah is divine protection.
quranUsage: 'There is no protector ('asim) today from Allah's command.' I'tasama is to hold fast.
notes: 'Ismah of prophets means their protection from major sins.

quranUsage: 'If you had been harsh (ghalizh).' Ghilzah is harshness. Ghaliz is harsh.
notes: The Prophet was not harsh - it would have driven people away.

quranUsage: 'We gave him glad tidings of a boy (ghulam).' Ghulam is boy/youth.
notes: Ibrahim and Zakariyya were given glad tidings of sons.

extendedMeaning: Ransoming, redeeming, or sacrificing for someone.
quranUsage: Fida' (فداء) is ransom. 'We ransomed (fadaynahu) him with a great sacrifice.' Fidyah is compensation.
notes: Ibrahim's son was ransomed with a ram.

quranUsage: Afwah (أفواه) is mouths. 'A word that comes out of their mouths (afwahihim).'

extendedMeaning: Loan, lending, and cutting off (a piece).
quranUsage: 'Who will loan Allah a goodly loan (qard)?' Qard is loan.
notes: Giving to Allah is described as lending Him - guaranteed return.

extendedMeaning: Humble devotion and prolonged standing in worship. Qunut is devoted obedience.
quranUsage: Qanit describes one who is devoutly obedient. Qunut prayers are prayers of humble supplication.

extendedMeaning: Stars in the sky and plants emerging from earth share the concept of 'appearing.'
quranUsage: An-Najm (The Star) is Surah 53. Stars guide travelers. 'The star and trees prostrate.'
notes: Najm originally means anything that appears/emerges.

extendedMeaning: Giving sincere, genuine advice for someone's benefit.
quranUsage: 'I convey to you my Lord's message and advise (ansah) you.' Nasihah is sincere counsel.
notes: Religion is nasihah (sincere advice) - hadith.

extendedMeaning: A specific, appointed time. Everything has its decreed moment.
quranUsage: Waqt is appointed time. Mawaqeet are fixed times (for prayer, Hajj). Miqat is the appointed place/time.
notes: Prayer times are mawaqeet - fixed appointments with Allah.

extendedMeaning: Losing hope, despair, or giving up.
quranUsage: Ya's (يأس) is despair. 'Do not despair (tay'asu) of Allah's mercy.' Ya'is is one who despairs.
notes: Despair of Allah's mercy is a sin.

quranUsage: 'Those who are miserly (yabkhalun) and enjoin miserliness.' Bukhl is miserliness.
notes: Miserliness is condemned; generosity is praised.

extendedMeaning: Early morning, virginity, or being first.
quranUsage: Bukrah (بكرة) is early morning. Bikr is virgin. 'Neither virgin (bikr) nor previously married.'

extendedMeaning: Whiteness, eggs (white things), and becoming white/bright.
quranUsage: 'His hand emerged white (bayda').' Abyad is white. Bayd is eggs.
notes: Musa's hand turning white was a sign. White symbolizes purity.

quranUsage: Jibah is forehead. 'Their foreheads (jibahuhum), sides and backs will be branded.'

extendedMeaning: Denying something known to be true.
quranUsage: Jahada means to deny. 'They denied (jahadu) Our signs.' Juhud is denial.
notes: Juhud is denying truth while knowing it.

quranUsage: Hasrah (حسرة) is regret. 'Alas (hasrata) for me!' Hasir is one full of regret.
notes: Hasrah is intense regret on Day of Judgment.

extendedMeaning: Inclining away from falsehood toward truth.
quranUsage: Hanif (حنيف) is one inclining to truth. 'Ibrahim was hanif (upright), not of the polytheists.'
notes: Hanifiyyah is the pure religion of Ibrahim.

quranUsage: Kharra means to fall prostrate. 'They fall (yakhirruna) on their faces prostrating.'

extendedMeaning: Addressing, giving sermon, and important matter.
quranUsage: 'What is your matter (khatb)?' Khutbah is sermon. Khitab is address.
notes: Khutbah is the Friday sermon.

primaryMeaning: to plunge, engage in vain talk
extendedMeaning: Plunging into something, especially vain discourse.
quranUsage: Khawda means to engage in vain talk. 'They were plunging (yakhuduuna) with those who plunge.'
notes: Idle, vain discourse is condemned.

quranUsage: Adraka means to reach/comprehend. 'Vision cannot perceive (tudrikuhu) Him.' Darak is lowest level.
notes: Darak is the lowest depth of Hell.

quranUsage: 'They feared (yarhabun) none but Allah.' Rahbah is fear. Rahib is monk.
notes: Monks (ruhban) dedicate themselves from fear of Allah.

quranUsage: 'O my two companions of the prison (sijn).' Sijn is prison.
notes: Yusuf was imprisoned unjustly but remained patient.

quranUsage: Safar is journey. Asfar are books/scriptures. Musafir is traveler.
notes: Travel is a form of unveiling (revealing new things).

extendedMeaning: Inserting, traveling a path, or following a way.
quranUsage: Salaka means to travel/insert. 'Travel (usluk) your hand into your garment.' Suluk is conduct.
'It was made to appear (shubiha) to them' - about Isa. Mutashabih is ambiguous.
notes: Some Quran verses are clear (muhkam), others ambiguous (mutashabih).

quranUsage: Shaqiy (شقي) is wretched. 'As for those who are wretched (shaquu).' Shaqawah is wretchedness.
notes: Opposite of sa'id (happy/blessed).

quranUsage: 'Those of the left (shimal).' Shimal is left/north. Shamil is comprehensive.
notes: Companions of the left are those destined for punishment.

quranUsage: 'Into sects (shiya').' Shi'ah is sect/party. Ishaah is spreading.
notes: Humanity divided into different groups.

extendedMeaning: Eager desire, can be positive (hoping for mercy) or negative (greed).
quranUsage: 'They hope (yatma'una) for His mercy.' Tama' is eager desire. Matma' is object of desire.
notes: Tama' in Allah's mercy is encouraged; tama' for worldly things leads to trouble.

quranUsage: 'We created man from clay (tin).' Tin is clay. Tinat is clay/nature.
notes: Adam was created from clay - our origin is humble.

quranUsage: 'Udhr (عذر) is excuse. 'What is your excuse ('udhrukum)?' Ma'dhirah is excuse.
notes: Some excuses are not accepted.

quranUsage: 'Usr (عسر) is difficulty. 'With difficulty ('usr) comes ease.' 'Asir is difficult.
notes: Allah promises ease after hardship.

extendedMeaning: A staff or stick. Also disobedience.
quranUsage: 'Asa (عصا) is staff. 'Throw your 'asa (staff)!' - Musa's staff. 'Asaa also means disobeyed.
notes: Musa's staff turned into a serpent.

quranUsage: 'Awn (عون) is help. 'We seek Your help (nasta'in).' Isti'anah is seeking help.
notes: Help is sought only from Allah.

quranUsage: Kannah is daughter-in-law. Kanna is to protect/conceal.
notes: Marriage creates new family bonds.

quranUsage: 'We clothed the bones with flesh (lahm).' 'Do you like to eat your brother's flesh?'
notes: Backbiting is compared to eating dead brother's flesh.

extendedMeaning: Throwing away, casting aside, or rejecting.
quranUsage: Nabadha means to cast away. 'They threw (nabadhuhu) it behind their backs.'
notes: Refers to rejecting the Book of Allah.

quranUsage: 'We created man from a drop (nutfah).' Nutfah is sperm drop.
notes: Human creation begins from a tiny drop.

extendedMeaning: Clear, articulate speech. The faculty of reason and expression.
quranUsage: Nutq is articulate speech. 'He does not speak (yantiq) from desire.' Mantiq is logic.
notes: Humans are 'hayawan natiq' - speaking/rational animals.

quranUsage: Nala/yanalu means to attain. 'Their meat does not reach (yanalu) Allah.' Nayl is attainment.
'In the sacred valley (wadi) of Tuwa.' Wadi is valley.
notes: Musa was called in the valley of Tuwa.

quranUsage: 'Those who join (yasilun) what Allah commanded to be joined.' Wasl is connection. Silah is maintaining ties.
notes: Silat ar-Rahim - maintaining family ties - is commanded.

quranUsage: Ayyada means to support. 'We supported (ayyadnahu) him with the Holy Spirit.'
notes: Isa was supported with Ruh al-Qudus.

extendedMeaning: Camel, beauty, and totality. The camel represents patience and endurance.
quranUsage: 'Do they not look at the camel (ibil) - how it is created?' Jamal is camel. Jamil is beautiful.
notes: The same root gives both 'camel' (jamal) and 'beautiful' (jamil).

extendedMeaning: War and warfare. State of hostility.
quranUsage: Harb is war. 'Those who wage war (yuharibun) against Allah and His Messenger.' Mihrab is prayer niche (place of spiritual battle).
notes: Interest-dealers are described as being at war with Allah.

extendedMeaning: Counting precisely, calculating. Hasa are pebbles (used for counting).
quranUsage: 'He has enumerated (ahsa) everything in number.' Ihsa' is precise counting.
notes: Allah counts all things - nothing escapes His knowledge.

quranUsage: 'Mothers breastfeed (yurdi'na) their children.' Rada'ah is breastfeeding.
notes: Breastfeeding creates milk-kinship (rada'ah).

extendedMeaning: Scriptures, writings, or pieces of iron.
quranUsage: Zubur (زبر) are scriptures. 'We gave Dawud the Zabur.' Zubar is pieces of iron.
notes: Zabur is the scripture given to Dawud.

quranUsage: Sabab (سبب) is cause/means. 'We gave him means (asbab) to everything.' Asbab are means.

extendedMeaning: Clouds and the action of dragging/pulling.
quranUsage: Sahab (clouds) are driven by wind and carry rain. 'Heavy clouds (sahab)' bring water.
notes: Clouds being 'dragged' across the sky is imagery used.

quranUsage: 'The foolish (sufaha') among the people.' Safah is foolishness. Safih is fool.
notes: Fools waste their wealth and reject guidance.

extendedMeaning: Fear mixed with compassion, or the reddish twilight.
quranUsage: Shafaq (شفق) is twilight/fear. 'By the shafaq (twilight).' Mushfiq is fearful/compassionate.

extendedMeaning: Being struck by a thunderbolt or fainting.
quranUsage: Sa'iqah (صاعقة) is thunderbolt. 'The sa'iqah (thunderbolt) struck them.' Sa'iq is one struck.
Taba'a means to seal. 'Allah has sealed (taba'a) their hearts.' Tab' is seal/nature.
notes: Hearts are sealed due to disbelief.

extendedMeaning: Edge, side, or a glance of the eye.
quranUsage: Tarf (طرف) is glance. 'Restricting their glances (tarf).' Taraf is edge/side.
'By the sky and the night-comer (tariq).' Tariq is knocker/night-comer.
notes: The tariq (star) knocks at night's door.

quranUsage: 'By the Mount (Tur)!' Tur is Mount Sinai. Tawr is stage.
notes: Mount Tur/Sinai is where Musa received revelation.

quranUsage: 'Gardens of grapes ('inab).' 'From it you take intoxicant and good provision.'
notes: Grapes are mentioned among Paradise fruits.

extendedMeaning: Grief, distress, or covering like clouds.
quranUsage: Ghamm (غم) is grief/distress. 'Grief upon grief (ghamman).' Ghammam is clouds.
'Those who restrain their anger (ghayz).' Ghayz is rage.
notes: Controlling rage is praiseworthy.

quranUsage: Ayy (أي) means which. 'Which (fa-bi-ayyi) of your Lord's favors will you deny?'
notes: Repeated in Surah Ar-Rahman.

quranUsage: Farra means to flee. 'So flee (firru) to Allah.' Firar is fleeing.
notes: Fleeing to Allah means turning to Him.

quranUsage: 'Lofty palaces (qusur).' Qasr is palace. Qasr also means shortening prayer.
notes: Travelers can shorten (qasr) their prayers.

quranUsage: 'They turn away from vain talk (laghw).' Laghw is vain speech.
notes: Believers avoid laghw - idle, meaningless talk.

extendedMeaning: Arriving, especially at water. Also rose.
quranUsage: Warada means to come to. 'Every one of you will arrive (wariduhaa) at it.' Wird is portion of worship.
notes: Everyone will come to Hell, but believers will pass.

quranUsage: Waqud (وقود) is fuel. 'Whose fuel (waqud) is people and stones.' Awqada is to kindle.

extendedMeaning: Leaning on, relying upon, or trusting.
quranUsage: Tawakkul is reliance. 'Upon Allah let the believers rely (yatawakkal).' Mutawakkil relies on Allah.
notes: Tawakkul is complete reliance on Allah.

quranUsage: 'We caused the sea (yamm) to engulf them.' Yamm is sea. Tayammum is dry ablution.
notes: Pharaoh was cast into the yamm (sea).

quranUsage: Asl (أصل) is root. 'Its root (asluha) firm and its branches in the sky.'
notes: The good word is like a good tree with firm roots.

quranUsage: Batasha means to seize. 'When you seize (batashtum), you seize like tyrants.' Batsh is violent seizing.

extendedMeaning: Compelling, mending, or being mighty and powerful.
quranUsage: Jabbar (جبار) is the Compeller - Allah's name. Also tyrant. 'He was not a jabbar (tyrant).'
notes: Al-Jabbar is one of Allah's names.

extendedMeaning: Being new, renewing, and being serious.
quranUsage: 'A new (jadid) creation.' Jadid is new. Tajdid is renewal.
notes: Allah can create anew - resurrection is a new creation.

quranUsage: Haqa means to befall. 'Evil plotting surrounds (yahiqu) only its own people.'
'Allah repels (yadfa'u) by some people.' Daf' is pushing/repelling.
notes: Allah uses some people to repel corruption from others.

quranUsage: Dammara means to destroy. 'We destroyed (dammarnaa) them utterly.' Tadmir is destruction.
Dam' (دمع) is tears. 'Their eyes overflow with tears (dam').'
Rijz (رجز) is punishment/abomination. 'We will send upon them rijz (punishment).' Also idols are rijz.
'Avoid the abomination (rijs) of idols.' Intoxicants are called rijs.
notes: Rijs covers physical and spiritual abominations.

quranUsage: Ra'a means to tend. 'They do not observe (yar'awna) any covenant.'
Rahiqa means to cover. 'Humiliation will cover (tarhaquha) them.' Irhaq is overburdening.

extendedMeaning: Drawing near, nearness, or stages of nearness.
quranUsage: Zulfa (زلفى) is nearness. 'That which brings us near (zulfa) to Allah.' Azlafa is to bring near.
Zayyala means to separate. 'We would have separated (zayyalna) them.'
'We returned him to the lowest (asfal) of the low.' Sufla is lower. Asfal is lowest.
notes: Humans can sink to the lowest of the low through disbelief.

extendedMeaning: Blackness, becoming black, and being a master/chief (sayyid).
quranUsage: 'On the Day when faces will be white and faces will be black (taswaddu).' Aswad is black. Sayyid is master.
notes: Sayyid (master/chief) shares this root - perhaps from authority's gravity.

quranUsage: 'She laughed (dahikat)' - Sarah at news of Ishaq. 'Let them laugh little.'
notes: Excessive laughing hardens the heart.

extendedMeaning: Losing something or wasting it. Being lost or neglected.
quranUsage: 'Allah does not waste (yudi'u) the reward of those who do good.' Diya' is loss/waste.
notes: Good deeds are never lost with Allah.

extendedMeaning: Length, being long, and bestowing favor.
quranUsage: 'Owner of favor (tawl).' Tul is length. Tawil is long.
notes: Al-Tawl refers to Allah's abundant favor.

quranUsage: 'Ata means to be insolent. 'They exceeded in 'utuww (insolence).' 'Atiyy is rebellious.
'Azala means to isolate. 'When you withdraw (i'tazaltum) from them.' I'tizal is withdrawal.
'The Holy Spirit (Ruh al-Qudus).' Quds is holiness. Muqaddas is sacred.
notes: Al-Quddus (The Holy) is one of Allah's names.

quranUsage: Qahhar (قهار) is the Subduer - Allah's name. 'Al-Wahid al-Qahhar.' Qahr is subjugation.
notes: Al-Qahhar is one of Allah's names.

quranUsage: 'Zakariyya took charge (kaffalaha) of her.' Kafalah is sponsorship.
notes: Zakariyya was Maryam's guardian.

quranUsage: Mi'ah (مائة) is hundred. 'Strike each of them with a hundred (mi'ata) lashes.'
Amla means to dictate. 'Let him who has the debt dictate (yumlil).' Imla' is dictation.
'We reduce (nanqusu) it from its edges.' Naqs is decrease/deficiency.
notes: Life and provisions can be decreased as a test.

quranUsage: 'He scattered (baththa) therein all kinds of creatures.' Bathth is spreading.
notes: Allah scattered diverse creatures across the earth.

quranUsage: Baraza means to appear. 'They will appear (barazuu) before Allah.'

extendedMeaning: Cattle/cows, and splitting open (cows split the earth plowing).
quranUsage: 'A yellow cow (baqarah), bright in color.' Baqar is cattle. Baqarah is cow.
notes: Surah Al-Baqarah is named after the cow in Musa's story.

quranUsage: 'A trade (tijarah) that will never perish.' Tijarah is trade. Tajir is merchant.
notes: The best trade is with Allah - faith for Paradise.

quranUsage: 'We said: Burn (harriqu) him!' Harq is burning. Hariq is fire.
notes: They tried to burn Ibrahim but fire became cool.

quranUsage: 'Bracelets of gold (huliy).' Hilyah is ornament.
notes: Paradise dwellers will be adorned with gold and pearls.

quranUsage: 'It seemed (yukhayyalu) to him from their magic.' Khayal is imagination. Khayl is horses.
notes: Magic creates illusions that seem real.

quranUsage: Da'im is continuous. 'Fruits continuous (da'im).' Dawam is permanence.
'So pray to your Lord and sacrifice (wanhar).' Dhabh is slaughter. Dhabiha is sacrifice.
notes: Proper slaughter (dhabh) makes meat halal.

quranUsage: 'You did not throw when you threw, but Allah threw.' Ramy is throwing.
notes: At Badr, the Prophet threw dust but Allah directed it.

quranUsage: Zina (زنى) is adultery/fornication. 'Do not approach zina.' Zani is fornicator.
notes: Zina is a major sin.

quranUsage: Zagha means to deviate. 'When they deviated (zaghu), Allah caused their hearts to deviate.' Zaygh is deviation.
Sabt (سبت) is Sabbath. 'Those who violated the Sabt (Sabbath).'
notes: Refers to the story of the Sabbath-breakers.

quranUsage: Saraqa means to steal. 'The male thief (sariq) and female thief.' Sariqah is theft.
'In honored scriptures (suhuf).' Sahifah is page. Suhuf is scriptures.
notes: Suhuf Ibrahim - the scriptures of Ibrahim.

quranUsage: 'To Him ascends (yas'adu) the good word.' Su'ud is ascending.
notes: Good words and deeds ascend to Allah.

extendedMeaning: Crossing, passing over, or interpreting dreams.
quranUsage: 'Abara means to interpret. 'If you can interpret (ta'buruuna) visions.' 'Ibrah is lesson.
'Araja means to ascend. 'The angels and the Spirit ascend (ta'ruju) to Him.' Ma'arij are ways of ascent.
'Azm (عزم) is resolve. 'Those of firm resolve ('ulul-'azm) among the messengers.' 'Azama is to determine.
notes: Ulul-'azm are the five greatest prophets.

extendedMeaning: Devotion, spiritual retreat, and staying in mosque.
quranUsage: 'While you are in devotion (akifun) in the mosques.' I'tikaf is spiritual retreat.
notes: I'tikaf in mosque, especially in Ramadan's last ten days.

extendedMeaning: Neck - connection between head and body.
quranUsage: 'Shackles on their necks ('anaq).' 'Unuq is neck.
notes: Freeing a neck (raqabah) means freeing a slave.

quranUsage: 'No crookedness ('iwaj) therein' - describing the Quran. A'waj is crooked.
notes: The Quran is perfectly straight with no deviation.

quranUsage: Sabaha/ya'um means to swim. 'Each in an orbit floating (yasbahun).'
Ghanam (غنم) is sheep. Ghanimah is spoils of war. 'Know that whatever you obtain as ghanima...'
'We opened (farrajna) it.' Faraj is relief. Farj is opening/gap.
notes: Allah provides relief from every difficulty.

quranUsage: 'Vessels of silver (fiddah).' Fiddah is silver. Infadda is to scatter.
notes: Silver vessels serve drinks in Paradise.

quranUsage: 'Their eyes overflow (tafidu) with tears.' Fayd is overflow.
notes: Eyes overflow with tears from emotion.

quranUsage: 'Allah takes (yaqbidu) the souls at death.' Qabd is grasping. Qabdah is handful.
notes: The Angel of Death grasps souls at their appointed time.

quranUsage: Qadhafa means to throw/accuse. 'We cast (naqdhifu) the truth against falsehood.' Also false accusation.
'Those who hoard (yaknizun) gold and silver.' Kanz is treasure. Iknaz is hoarding.
notes: Hoarding wealth without paying zakat is condemned.

quranUsage: 'Of various colors (alwan).' Lawn is color. Mulawwan is colored/varied.
notes: Diversity of colors in creation is a sign of Allah.

extendedMeaning: Breaking something, especially covenants or contracts.
quranUsage: 'Those who break (yanqudun) Allah's covenant.' Naqd is breaking/undoing.
notes: Covenant-breakers are condemned repeatedly.

extendedMeaning: Sleep as rest and temporary death.
quranUsage: Nawm is sleep. 'Neither drowsiness nor sleep (nawm) overtakes Him.' Sleep is called 'minor death.'
notes: Allah neither sleeps nor drowses (Ayat al-Kursi).

extendedMeaning: Intending, being about to, or worry.
quranUsage: Hamma means to intend. 'She intended (hammat) him and he intended her.' Hamm is worry/intention.

extendedMeaning: Heaviness in ears, or dignity and reverence.
quranUsage: Waqr (وقر) is heaviness. 'In their ears is waqr (deafness).' Waqar is dignity.
Wahn (وهن) is weakness. 'Do not weaken (tahinu) or grieve.' Wahin is weak.
Ana (آنى) is time/hour. Inaa' (إناء) is vessel. 'From vessels (aniyah) of silver.'
An (أن) can indicate time. 'Idha' is 'when.'
'Bring your proof (burhan).' Burhan is proof.
notes: Claims require burhan (proof).

quranUsage: Buhtan (بهتان) is slander. 'A clear buhtan (slander).' Bahata is to astonish.
Mutraf (مترف) is one living in luxury. 'We sent a warner to any town except that its mutrafun (affluent) said...'
'Speak to them from behind a veil (hijab).' Hijab is screen/veil.
notes: Hijab provides modesty and protection.

quranUsage: 'Seal (khatam) of the Prophets.' 'Allah sealed (khatama) their hearts.'
notes: Muhammad is the final Prophet - the seal.

extendedMeaning: Sinking into earth, or lunar eclipse.
quranUsage: Khasafa means to sink. 'We caused the earth to swallow (khasafna) him.' Khusuf is eclipse.
'Reclining on green (khudur) cushions.' Akhdar is green. Khadir is verdant.
notes: Green is associated with Paradise and life. Al-Khidr's name means 'the green one.'

quranUsage: 'Five (khamsah) of them.' Khamsah is five. Khamis is Thursday (fifth day).
notes: Five daily prayers, five pillars of Islam.

quranUsage: 'Your maternal uncles (khwal).' Khal is maternal uncle.
notes: Maternal relatives have special status in Islam.

quranUsage: 'A sign (dalil) guiding them.' Dalil is proof/guide. Dalalah is indication.
notes: Evidence (dalil) guides to truth.

quranUsage: Rajfah (رجفة) is earthquake/trembling. 'The rajfah (earthquake) seized them.' Rajif is trembling.

extendedMeaning: Desiring something (raghiba fi) or turning away from (raghiba 'an).
quranUsage: 'To their Lord they turn in desire (yarghabun).' Raghbah is desire.
notes: Can mean desire toward or aversion from, depending on preposition.

quranUsage: 'Created the heavens and earth in six (sittah) days.' Sittah is six.
notes: Creation in six days demonstrates Allah's power and wisdom.

quranUsage: Asra means to travel by night. 'Glory to Him who took His servant by night (asra).' Isra' is the night journey.
notes: The Prophet's night journey to Jerusalem.

quranUsage: Saqata means to fall. 'When it fell (suqita) into their hands.' Saqit is one who falls.
'What has passed (salafa) is forgiven.' Salaf are predecessors.
notes: The righteous Salaf are the early generations of Muslims.

extendedMeaning: Forgiving by turning away from offense.
quranUsage: 'Turn away (safh) graciously.' Safh is gracious forgiveness.
notes: Gracious forgiveness ignores the offense entirely.

quranUsage: 'I will crucify (la-usallibannakum) you.' Salb is crucifixion. Sulb is hard/loins.
notes: Pharaoh threatened to crucify those who believed.

quranUsage: 'Lower your voice (sawt).' Sawt is sound/voice.
notes: Lowering one's voice shows respect and humility.

quranUsage: Tadarru' (تضرع) is humble supplication. 'Call upon your Lord with humility (tadarru'an).'

extendedMeaning: Hamstringing an animal, or being barren.
quranUsage: 'Aqara means to hamstring. 'They hamstrung ('aqaru) the she-camel.' 'Aqir is barren.

extendedMeaning: Living, life, or means of living.
quranUsage: 'Aysh (عيش) is life/living. Ma'ishah is livelihood. 'We distributed their livelihood (ma'ishatahum).'
'Covered with dust (ghabarah).' Ghubar is dust.
notes: Faces will be covered with dust on Judgment Day.

quranUsage: Farrata means to neglect. 'What I neglected (farrattu) regarding Allah.' Ifrat is excess.
'When the graves (qubur) are overturned.' Qabr is grave. Maqbarah is cemetery.
notes: The graves will release their contents on Judgment Day.

extendedMeaning: Burdening, charging with duty, or obligation.
quranUsage: Kallafa means to burden. 'Allah does not burden (yukallifu) a soul beyond its capacity.' Taklif is obligation.

extendedMeaning: Subtle kindness, gentle care. Perceiving and handling delicate matters.
